instruction: Apply blue font color throughout the document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing all text color to blue (RGB: 0, 0, 255) throughout the document. The evaluator uses a custom getter to extract all font colors and a custom metric to verify all colors are blue (within tolerance of 30 for color variations). The postconfig saves the file to ensure formatting changes persist.

llm_judge_reasons: Comprehensive document coverage: Getter correctly checks all major document elements including paragraph runs (lines 33-38), table cells (lines 41-49), headers (lines 54-60), and footers (lines 63-69). This covers 'throughout the entire document' requirement.

Correct metric logic: Metric properly handles expected parameter (expected.get('target_color')) without incorrectly accessing expected.get('rules'), correctly implements color tolerance comparison (within 30 for each RGB channel), and verifies ALL extracted colors match target blue [0,0,255].
Proper postconfig: Saves document via Ctrl+S to persist color changes before verification, ensuring getter reads the modified file state.
Expected value correct: Target color [0,0,255] is correct RGB for blue.

Minor limitation: Getter only captures text with explicit color formatting (run.font.color.rgb check on line 35). If document has text with default/automatic color that wasn't changed to blue, it won't be captured. However, when user actively changes text to blue in LibreOffice, explicit RGB is added, so this should work correctly for completed tasks.

Edge case: Returns 0.0 if no colors found (metric line 24-25), which is appropriate since changing text to blue should create explicit colors. Would correctly fail if document is empty or no text was changed.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that document contains text before checking colors, to provide clearer failure message for empty documents.

Could add check for text without explicit colors to detect incomplete color changes, but this may be overly strict since the task requires changing ALL text to blue (which would add explicit formatting).
